blocks.text: Network models explain how data moves from one device to another in an organised way. They divide communication into layers, and each layer performs a specific task in data transmission (Fig 1.13). Layered models make networks easier to understand and manage, help in troubleshooting, and are used as standards in networking.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: Network models are used to understand complex network communication in simple steps.

Network layers divide the communication process into smaller parts, each with a specific responsibility. Data passes through the layers step by step. This makes network design simple and organised: a change in one layer does not affect the other layers, and layered communication improves reliability and control.

The OSI model is a standard seven-layer model used to understand network communication. Each layer performs a different function. It is used for learning and designing networks, and it helps different systems communicate properly. On the sender, data passes down from the application layer to the physical layer; on the receiver it passes back up.

blocks.alt: The OSI model on the sender side: a sender computer beside seven stacked layers, Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical, with arrows pointing down; a cable leaves the Physical layer and a dashed line leads to a receiver computer marked for context.
blocks.caption: Figure 1.13: OSI Model on the Sender Side Showing Data Flow from the Application Layer to the Physical Layer (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 1.13).

items: Physical layer: sends raw data as electrical, optical or radio signals over the medium; defines hardware aspects such as cables, connectors, voltage levels and data rates.
Data link layer: ensures error-free transfer between directly connected nodes; handles framing, error detection and correction, and access to the shared medium.
Network layer: routes data from source to destination across different networks; manages logical addressing (IP addresses) and chooses the best path.
Transport layer: provides reliable, ordered delivery between devices; performs error recovery, flow control and segmentation of data into smaller units.
Session layer: establishes, maintains and terminates communication sessions between applications; manages checkpoints and recovery after interruptions.
Presentation layer: translates data into a format the application layer understands; handles encryption, compression and format conversion.
Application layer: provides services directly to users and applications; supports protocols such as HTTP, FTP and email.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text: Lower layers handle the physical transfer of data, middle layers manage routing and delivery, and upper layers support user applications. Each layer works independently, and together they ensure proper communication.
